question: Why can we still detect radiation at Chernobyl today?
answer: The short-lived atoms burned out fast. Cesium-137 and strontium-90 last for decades and are still in the soil, so the Geiger counter still clicks. Take them out and it goes quiet.
move: Contamination lasts as long as its longest-lived atoms.

web.label: A year slider from 1986 to 2020 sits over a Geiger counter reading at Chernobyl. Dragging the years shows the counter clicking until the long-lived cesium and strontium are removed, then going quiet.
